messages:
maria (product): Heads-up — BigLogo is escalating. They want a formal 99.9% request-level SLA and a guaranteed latency p95 for inference for renewal. Renewal in 28 days. They say this is deal-breaker.

jess (sales): They called this morning. Finance + engineering are both on the renewal call next week. They asked if we can ship an SLA + low-latency profile before renewal.

alex (cs): Context: they run high-throughput customer workflows. They’re currently on shared hosted with spikes causing tail latency. We recommended Dedicated but they want hosted SLA first.

sam (eng lead): Technical reality: adding a formal 99.9% per-request SLA on hosted requires routing guarantees, capacity reservations, and an eval of fallback policies. Minimal effort workaround is offering Dedicated/Reserved capacity + canary rollout which we already support. Building hosted SLA features is non-trivial (capacity isolation + billing/automation).

maria (product): We need to decide: negotiate contractual workaround (discount + Dedicated offer) vs re-prioritizing hosted SLA work now. Use RICE/impact-effort to guide.

devon (vp product): Quick RICE take: Impact = high (deal value + precedence), Reach = medium, Confidence = medium (we can deliver infra, but ops risk), Effort = very high. Score likely favors a short-term commercial workaround.

olivia (acct mgr): Renewal value is $900k ARR. If we lose, churn risk cascades into references. Sales asks for a deployable proposition that looks like an SLA on paper within 2 weeks.

sam (eng lead): Options: 1) Prioritize hosted SLA engineering (6-10 wks) — high effort, long-term value. 2) Offer Dedicated pilot + temporary SLA/credit (1 week legal/ops) — low effort, immediate. 3) Provide a documented SLO + technical mitigations (KV caching, prefilling, request routing) and promise roadmap slot — medium effort.

jess (sales): Sales prefers option 2 now (Dedicated + temporary SLA) to close renewal then push hosted SLA as roadmap item.

maria (product): Tradeoffs: option 2 closes deal fast but sets expectation that hosted SLA is 'coming' — could spawn more similar asks. Option 1 solves long-term but risks losing deal. Need launch criteria and guardrails if we promise hosted SLA later.

alex (cs): If we go with Dedicated pilot, CS can commit to 2-week ramp and a runbook. We can also offer a one-time SLA credit clause in contract while engineering roadmap delivers permanent solution.

devon (vp product): My recommendation: short-term commercial + Dedicated pilot to secure renewal. Immediately create a prioritized 6-week project to harden hosted SLA with milestones + QA gate. Use impact vs effort to sequence features: capacity isolation > routing policies > billing automation.

sam (eng lead): Agree sequencing. Proposed epics and rough estimates: capacity isolation (3w), routing + fallback (2w), billing + legal hooks (1w). Total ~6w. Need 2 engineers + SRE on-call.

maria (product): Action items: 1) jess/olivia finalize renewal wording offering Dedicated pilot + temporary SLA credit (due EOD). 2) sam build initial epic card + staffing request (by tomorrow). 3) devon approve 6-week priority slot and resource commit (by Friday). 4) alex prepare CS ramp runbook.

jess (sales): I’ll draft contract clause: 8-week Dedicated pilot, 30-day SLA credit if we miss p95, and a timeline for hosted SLA delivery.

olivia (acct mgr): I’ll communicate to customer that Dedicated path is fastest and we’ll include roadmap transparency.

sam (eng lead): I’ll open the GitHub epic and add estimates.

maria (product): If any objections to plan, flag now. Otherwise I’ll post this as the source of truth for the renewal war room.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging at 2026-03-20T15:30:00Z

devon (vp product): No objections from me. Prioritize this delivery and keep exec updated.

maria (product): Thanks — I’ll start the war room thread and ping legal for the contract language.
